about: This Grinds My Gears template shows Peter Griffin from Family Guy behind a news desk, teeth clenched and hands raised in angry exasperation, next to a yellow graphic of two interlocking cogs reading "What Really Grinds My Gears". In the show Peter hosts a short opinion segment on the local news where he rants about petty annoyances with complete outrage. The meme carries that energy: a tiny, oddly specific pet peeve announced as if it were a national scandal.
origin: The bit comes from Family Guy, where Peter's news segment of the same name lets him air trivial grievances on air. The phrase itself is an older English idiom for something that irritates you.
usage:
The top box is the setup, usually Peter's catchphrase asking what really grinds his gears. The bottom box names the pet peeve, starting with "when" or "people who".

The more trivial and specific the complaint, the funnier the fury. Think coworkers replying-all, gamers who pause cutscenes, shoppers who block the aisle. Keep the grievance short and relatable so readers nod along before they laugh.
